title: How many marbles do Ziva and Ruhee bring?
description: A child brings loose marbles and another child brings bags of marbles. A bracket shows that the bags are worked out first, and the total is found. Keeko doubts the order and adds the first two numbers before multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: a bracket tells us which part to work out first. Watch for children who work from left to right and add before multiplying.

source: Example 4: Ziva brought 30 marbles to the playground. Ruhee brought 5 bags of marbles with 4 marbles in each bag. How many marbles did they bring?
video_script.why: The child sees why an expression needs a bracket to show which part is worked out first.
video_script.substitution: Write the bags as a times part, put it in a bracket, and work out the bracket first.
video_script.anchor: Ziva's thirty marbles and Ruhee's five bags of four marbles at the field
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko works from left to right, adds thirty and five first, and then multiplies by four, which treats thirty five as the number of bags.
video_script.payoff_line: Ziva and Ruhee brought fifty marbles in all

final_answer.spoken: the expression is thirty plus five times four, which is the same as thirty plus the bracket, and the value is fifty marbles

names.Ziva: the child who brought 30 marbles to the playground
names.Ruhee: the child who brought 5 bags of 4 marbles

maths_rules: Ruhee brings 5 bags with 4 marbles in each bag, so 5 × 4 = 20 marbles.
slip: 30 + 5 = 35 and 35 × 4 = 140, which treats 35 as the bags
video_script.design: One idea: a bracket shows what is worked out first. Assumes multiplying equal lots. Wrong idea: work from left to right. The loose marbles and the five bags stay all video.

marks.ask: a question mark glows over the marbles

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>Ziva brought thirty marbles to the field.
<bookmark mark='bags'/>Ruhee brought five bags of marbles, with four marbles in each bag.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many marbles did they bring, and how do we write it?

beats.on_screen: the marbles stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a pair of curved lines ( ) drawn around the five bags, with the label bracket

marks.def: the curved lines appear around the five bags and the label bracket lands on them
marks.first: the part inside the lines glows

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>The curved lines written around part of an expression are called a bracket.
<bookmark mark='first'/>A bracket tells us to work out what is inside it first.

beats.on_screen: Given: 30 marbles; 5 bags with 4 marbles in each bag
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Ziva has thirty marbles, and Ruhee has five bags with four marbles in each.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression for all the marbles, and its value

marks.find: the words expression and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write an expression for all the marbles, and find its value.

marks.bags: 5 × 4 is written under the five bags

narration: <bookmark mark='bags'/>Step one, write the marbles in the bags. Five bags with four marbles each make five times four.

marks.write: the bracket is drawn around 5 × 4 and joined to 30 with a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step two, add the bags to the thirty. We put a bracket around five times four, so that part is worked out first.

marks.inside: 5 × 4 is worked out and replaced by 20

narration: <bookmark mark='inside'/>Step three, work out the bracket first. Five times four is twenty.

marks.add: the 30 and the 20 are joined with a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step four, add the twenty to the thirty, because the bracket is now one number.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Ziva and Ruhee brought fifty marbles in all.
The expression is thirty plus five times four, and it means thirty plus the bracket.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 30 + 5 = 35, then 35 × 4 = 140; five bags of 4 beside it do not match thirty five bags; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the five bags glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko adds thirty and five first, then multiplies by four.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But that makes thirty five bags of four marbles each, which is far too many. The bracket shows that five times four comes first.
